entry_points.text: Filter operation accepts only program-config and pool-config requests, dispatching each separately and rejecting others; config-change notification only schedules deferred work.
Probe picks queue pairs from device maximum when multiqueue or scaling is present else single, falls back to single when out of bounds or without control queue, and caps by online CPUs.
Module init establishes online and dead CPU hotplug states then registers the driver, unwinding on failure; exit unregisters then removes both states in reverse order.

Kernel console named hvc wires write, device and setup with buffered replay from invalid index and early registration, rejecting removed or out-of-range indexes; terminal ops cover install, open, close, write, hangup, throttle, room, modem and optional poll, port ops only destruct.

Early DCC probe spins boundedly for transmit drain then installs the write handler else reports absence; console and device init abort when the channel is absent, and device setup pins hotplug under SMP serialization then allocates console zero with 128-byte buffer.

IUCV transport handler maps pending, sever, completion and incoming-message events to line callbacks; console interrupt handler polls its console, kicks the service thread on repoll request, and always reports handled.

exports.text: Virtio network driver binds to the network device identifier with any sub-identifier, exposing probe, remove, validate, config-change and optional suspend and resume handlers with modern and legacy feature tables sized from themselves.

Device operations cover transmit, redirect transmit, socket wakeup, open and close, address handling, receive mode, statistics, VLAN, filter attach, feature audit and update, physical naming and timeout.
Driver exposes a read-only per-queue mergeable buffer length attribute and zero-copy metadata operations with only a receive-hash callback.
IRQ notifier helpers attach the console interrupt handler with instance flags, detach by freeing and clearing, and implement hangup as detach; IRQ zero means no request.

hazards.text: Mergeable size query traps unless the queue index lies within configured pairs; callers must never pass foreign queues.
MTU shrinking between validation and probe is fatal rather than clamped; scaling commit failure disables hash and reporting with a warning while the device stays usable.

Write checks open count without the port lock so racing close or hangup can change the outcome; room and buffered-count read size fields without the instance lock so concurrent staging can make them stale.
Console output retries with flush while the backend reports try-again and silently drops on other errors, risking stall under a stuck backend or message loss on persistent failure.
Presence probing emits a newline and spins with relaxed waiting; SMP serialization disables CPU hotplug pinning core zero, and work skipped while core zero is offline can leave queued bytes pending.

Receive keeps the head descriptor queued on payload allocation failure and reports memory shortage for retry; synchronous flush cancels delayed work, forces one send, then briefly waits for drain which may still be non-empty on timeout.

invariants.text: Validation requires a control queue whenever multiqueue, scaling, hash reporting, receive, VLAN, MAC, announce or coalescing capabilities appear; missing prerequisites are logged as failures, missing config access is rejected, undersized MTU and standby without MAC support are silently dropped, and clearing affects only the named recognized bit.

Guest segmentation is present when any IPv4, IPv6, congestion or legacy variant appears with UDP needing both families; large receive is enabled when MTU exceeds standard payload or any guest segmentation exists; checksum unlocks hardware checksum, scatter-gather and tunnel segmentation with robust segmentation and receive checksum always on; negotiated header prefers tunnel hash, then hash with reporting, then mergeable or modern, else legacy.

Scaling records indirection and key sizes clamped to driver maximum with warning, masks unsupported extension hash types, and enables hash plus metadata; hash toggling rewrites stored selection then commits with failure reported invalid; metadata hash needs receive-hash offload, locates the hash header by negotiated length, clamps unknown codes and returns value plus translated type covering IPv4, IPv6, extension, TCP and UDP variants.

Port naming reports standby only with that feature else unsupported including short buffers; GRO toggling is refused while filtering is active else reprogrammed with stored state updated only on success; timeout handling counts per-queue timeouts under sequence protection with queue identity and idle time; encap audit clears checksum caps for non-offloaded or still-segmenting packets; filter completion always resumes receive and transmit with prior state restored on failure.
Receive release drains all queued pages per queue and detaches any filter program with reference drop; idle send-queue cleanup resets transmit bookkeeping for the matching network queue.

Probed Ethernet enables high DMA, unicast filtering, live address change and bounded MTU with basic redirect and zero-copy plus scatter-gather when mergeable, using the device address when offered else random; probe sets true queue counts, page pools, per-queue moderation, mergeable sysfs grouping, default scaling and receive-mode handling plus failover when standby exists, aborting on creation failure; completion turns carrier off, learns link via config change when status exists else records up locally, and registers CPU notification after releasing the networking lock with failure causing full teardown in fixed unwind order.

Config reads may sleep; multi-element reads sample an optional generation counter before and after fetching each element and repeat until stable, single byte reads do one transport get, 16 and 32 bit reads convert device endian to host order, and byte arrays use the multi-element byte path.

Lookup by index walks under the global mutex, matches under each instance lock, and holds a port reference on success; flush invokes backend flush when present with console path never waiting and terminal path always waiting; instantiation validates range, removed slot and no existing user; install resolves by terminal index and manages the reference, cleanup drops it, and hangup cancels resize, zeroes count, clears terminal and output length and notifies the backend when present.

Write fails without driver data or opens, else stages into free tail space under the instance lock, pushes, flushes and yields while input remains, kicks the thread and reports staged bytes; room and buffered counts report free and filled tail space; window handling snapshots cached size under lock; modem get and set delegate to the backend; poll init always succeeds, fetch maps empty or error to no-character, store spins until one byte is accepted, and unthrottle only kicks.

Kernel console output ignores out-of-range or removed indexes, expands newline with carriage return, emits small aligned chunks, retries try-again with flush, compacts partial progress, discards on other errors and flushes at end; backend pointers and terminal numbers live in fixed arrays initially marked removed; globals hold kick, sysrq, last index and init-need counters plus driver and background task pointers.

DCC output spins while transmit-busy then emits one byte with block output repeating per byte; block input drains at most the requested bytes while receive-ready; presence probing emits a break, waits about a tenth of a second for idle, and latches a sticky flag letting non-zero cores short-circuit when SMP serialization is on.

Inbound retrieval reports idle when disconnected or empty and pipe error when severed, receives the head once, discards on transport error or version and length mismatch, copies with offset tracking and more-data signalling, applies window updates under console lock and ignores other control types; outbound counts drops silently while disconnected, fails when severed, else appends within free staging space and schedules delayed transmit, wrapping staged bytes into one data message and always clearing staging length.

Local hangup flushes synchronously then marks closed, cleaning only when already severed so established paths survive; remote sever marks severed and cleans when closed or for consoles else kicks; lowering modem signals flushes and forces disconnected with outside-lock teardown; delete flushes, destroys both queues and resets length; line lookup bounds-checks the index, wrappers come from a dedicated pool with zeroed metadata and versioned data payload, list destruction unlinks and frees each entry, and diagnostics carry a fixed prefix.

locks.text: Bulk receive release, moderation release and probe registration plus early programming serialize with the global routing config lock to exclude filter lookup, concurrent open and routing changes; moderation teardown is skipped without per-queue coalescing capability; control-queue mutex is initialized before use.
Config-change notification takes the device config lock with interrupts saved, invokes the internal change helper, then releases with interrupts restored.

A global mutex guards the console list during walk and unlink with each index compared under that instance lock; destruction holds the global mutex while taking the instance lock to unlink before freeing; open-count changes use the port lock and output staging plus window snapshots use the instance lock, both with interrupts saved.
A dedicated DCC spin lock guards input and output FIFOs and is always taken with interrupt state saved around FIFO movement and direct channel access.
The per-line spin lock protects state flags, staging length and both queues in process and bottom-half forms; path teardown always runs outside it due to ordering against the transport table lock.

state_machines.text: Config change first serves peer announcement when capable, then tracks link: unchanged is ignored, link up refreshes settings plus carrier on and queue wake, link down does carrier off and queue stop.

Common teardown resets the device, releases unused and receive buffers, resets transmit queues, destroys page pools and deletes queues; remove additionally stops CPU notification, flushes config and receive-mode work, frees moderation, unregisters and destroys failover; freeze stops notification, downs, then common teardown; restore brings up, restores queue count and re-adds notification, rolling back on failure.

Device ready is signalled only after successful registration with change notifications held off until open, after which queues are activated; coalescing and moderation defaults start at zero thresholds with transmit packet threshold derived from polling weight.

First open binds the terminal, attempts notifier registration, raises DTR when baud is configured, marks initialized and kicks even on failure; concurrent opens only bump count and kick; final close clears the terminal, lowers DTR when hangup-on-close is set, removes the notifier, cancels resize, waits bounded by close-wait, and clears initialized; negative count is an error.

The background thread is freezable with identity in a global pointer, clears the kick flag each round, polls every instance under the global mutex unless CPUs are in the debugger when it records read need, restarts immediately when kicked, sleeps until kicked when idle, else sleeps interruptibly with additive backoff from minimum toward maximum using distinct read and write need flags.

With SMP serialization off both DCC directions touch the channel directly; when on only core zero with empty FIFO touches directly, else output is appended and input drained via FIFOs with work scheduled on core zero; IUCV connection moves among disconnected, connected and severed while the tty moves between closed and opened, cleanup forces disconnected plus closed, and established connections survive tty hangup.

structs.text: Mergeable attributes form a single-entry null-terminated table exposed as a group under the short name; MTU limits follow Ethernet minimum and maximum; hash-report translation capacity is ten entries with out-of-range codes treated as none.

Base features cover checksum, segmentation, mergeable receive, status, control queue and related offloads; the modern table adds guest and host UDP tunnel segmentation variants including checksum variants, while legacy adds generic segmentation and any-layout support.

Each console instance anchors on a terminal port with a private spin lock, index, pending-output and wakeup sizing state, terminal number, backend operations pointer, interrupt and private fields, cached window size with deferred resize work, list linkage, flags and a trailing word-aligned flexible output area.

Backend operations group character fetch and store, optional flush with wait control, add, remove and hangup lifecycle notifiers, modem line get and set, and DTR plus RTS control, with several handlers optional and checked before use.

Console ABI uses major 229 minor 0, close-wait one tenth of a second, output and input chunks of sixteen, atomic read maximum 128, poll flags one for read and two for write, backoff from ten to two thousand milliseconds, sixteen consoles with eight preallocated adapters, and DCC status bits thirty for receive and twenty-nine for transmit with 128-byte input and 1024-byte output buffers.

Wire messages begin with one-byte version and type, a two-byte payload length and variable payload, packed with total size header plus length; protocol version is two, types are one error, two environment, four termios, eight window size and sixteen data, with maximum payload the largest unsigned sixteen-bit value.

Per-line state holds a console reference, eight-byte service name, console flag, connection and tty state, path pointer, spin lock, page-sized send buffer with length, delayed work with wait queue, outgoing and incoming lists, device pointer and path info; each queued wrapper links into a list, stores transport metadata, tracks a read offset and points at the wire buffer.

Send capacity is one page below maximum payload, queueing delays transmit by one twenty-fifth of a second, synchronous flush waits up to one tenth, console index is zero and default line count one; filtering allows up to five hundred eight-byte entries with star wildcard prefix matching and accepts all when unconfigured, with line table sized from adapter count and pool minimum from page size over wrapper size quartered.
